# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

**Iteration 3/5 · candidate `cand_0003` · parent: `cand_0001` (champion, val 0.925) · bar: paired
Δ̄ > 0.2·SE = 0.0124 (SE 0.0620, n=40)**

## The situation this iteration inherits

`cand_0002` **fixed all three remaining failures and broke three passing tasks**, netting exactly
0.000 and being reverted whole:

> RESULT: REJECTED · val=0.925 Δ=+0.000 · fixed={560-12, 59595, 9569} · broke={402-43, 50768, 80-42}

So the diagnosis this iteration is **not** "which tasks fail" — it is **"which sentence of cand_0002
moved which task"**. A 1:1 attribution is the whole deliverable, because the fixing text and the
breaking text were shipped as one batch. I built that attribution from the `cand_0002` trajectories
(which the framework copied into `rollouts/val/`, giving me the *post-edit* traces for all six moved
tasks) plus a direct `diff -u` of `candidates/cand_0001/*` against `candidates/cand_0002/*`.

## Attribution table — the actual ranked issue list

| task | moved | the text that moved it | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **59595** | 0→1 | Placeholder-discrimination **prose alone** (Rule 3 verdict row + Rule 2 non-parseable-string fact). Decisive proof: the agent wrote `if 4 <= r <= 19` in its **first** block, before any output file existed and with zero deliberation prose — so the `PLAN` machinery had not run yet and cannot be the cause. | **RESHIP, narrowed** |
| **9569** | 0→1 | Rule 2b's *"assign that value object through, unrounded"*. cand_0001 did `ans = round(float(v), 4)`; cand_0002 did `ans = v`. | **RESHIP, de-contaminated** |
| **560-12** | 0→1 | The **ANCHOR** text alone (the `PLAN`/`LEAVE` dict machinery was vacuous here). Note: the **seed also passed 560-12**, so `cand_0001` was a regression on it. | **RESHIP, narrowed** |
| **50768** | 1→0 | The **ANCHOR** text. Forced to print a prose `ANCHOR:` conclusion on an instruction that names no address, the agent invented a "matrix convention" and **transposed the axes**, overriding axis labels it had itself printed. | **cause removed** |
| **402-43** | 1→0 | The Rule 3 **verdict-table / PRE-FILLED rewrite**. With no pre-filled cells inside `answer_position` (Sheet2 absent), branch 3 sent the agent *hunting outside the box*; it found a `THE ABOVE TABLE WOULD BECOME:` illustration and copied that as the deliverable. | **cause removed** |
| **80-42** | 1→0 | **Deleting** *"leave the example cells as they are"* and adding the blanket bans *"never by which cells happen to be empty"* / *"never write `if cell.value is None`"*. cand_0001 passes 80-42 **by** that construct — the instruction says "into the first available, **blank** rows", so emptiness *is* the spec. Output came back byte-identical to input. | **cause removed** |

Tags: 59595 and 80-42 are **DECISION/PERMISSION** (same decision class — "is this pre-filled cell an
example or a placeholder?" — with *opposite* correct answers, which is exactly why cand_0002's
class-wide rewrite fixed one and broke the other). 9569 is **KNOWLEDGE**. 560-12/50768 are
**KNOWLEDGE** about where inside the box the answer goes, again with opposite failure directions.

**No ENVIRONMENT fault found.** Every one of the six moves is explained by text in the two editable
files; the grader and adapter behaved consistently across all three runs. Nothing outside
`prompt.md` and `task_template.md` was touched.

## Changes made this iteration (3 edits, all in the two editable files)

| # | cluster | edit class (skill §) | file(s) | what it says, and why it generalizes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **A** | 560-12 / 50768 | add a sourced rule + add the reason (§4, §2) + one `<example>` (§5) | `prompt.md` Rule 3 (2 bullets); `task_template.md` `answer_position` bullet + `<example>` | `answer_position` is a **bounding box**, so the answer has its own anchor inside it, by a 3-step precedence: a cell the instruction names *inside the box* → a place the instruction *describes* ("the first blank rows", "under the last entry") → else the box's top-left. **Plus the narrowing second bullet that is the whole point:** the anchor fixes only where the answer *starts*; which value lands in which row/column is fixed by **the labels the sheet prints along the box's edges** plus any orientation the instruction states, and you must never lay out a grid from a convention while the sheet labels its own axes. |
| **B** | 59595 / 80-42 | add a **narrowing condition** on an existing rule (§4) | `prompt.md` Rule 3; `task_template.md` Round 1 | Keeps *"leave the example cells as they are"* **verbatim**, and adds the discriminator: when a pre-filled cell **contradicts your rule**, look down the rest of its column. Marker recurs down the column → it is the table's absence convention, keep it. Marker is the **odd one out** among real computed entries → it is a placeholder for the value you were asked to compute, overwrite it. |
| **C** | 9569 | add a sourced rule + add the reason (§4, §2) | `prompt.md` Rule 2; `task_template.md` Round 1 + Round-3 point 4 | **Never round a value on its way into a cell**, *because* the grader rounds both sides to 2 dp itself, so your round is a **second** rounding and double rounding breaks ties the opposite way. Plus: a worked example's **digit count is not part of the spec** (owners type what their number format displays), so reproduce an example's *rule*, never its digit count — and "agreement you had to round to obtain is not agreement". |

### Dropped, and never to be re-introduced

All of these are `cand_0002` text that my attribution shows was **vacuous on all three fixes** while
being implicated in all three regressions:

- the Round-2 `PLAN` / `LEAVE` dict machinery and `assert set(PLAN) == set(CELLS)`;
- `assert not offplan` — on 9569 it **fired on float round-tripping noise**
  (`('AO79', '0.373369645', '0.37336964500000003')`) and cost a whole round; worse, its natural
  "fix" is to round, which is the exact failure Edit C forbids;
- the Round-3 restructure that hoisted `CELLS` into Round 1 and clipped with `ws.max_row` (the
  **input**, 3999 rows for 80-42) instead of `chk.max_row` (the **saved file**, 7997) — a latent bug
  that silently excludes an append destination from the checked range;
- the unconditional deletion of *"leave the example cells as they are"*;
- the blanket ban on `if cell.value is None`;
- the mandatory prose `ANCHOR:` print, and the `<example>` that was **task 560-12 verbatim**;
- Rule 2b's shipped *rationale* for the pre-filled-decimals paragraph, whose illustration was
  `0.1707` / `0.170687841` — literally AO9 and G9 of task 9569. I kept the principle and wrote it
  with no task's numbers in it, which is what makes it a general rule rather than a memorized answer.

## Verify-the-fix (one line per change, against the traces)

- **A, fixes 560-12** — `answer_position` is `'工作表1'!I2:J7` and the instruction says *"The answer
  should be put **from I3** with the Headers…"*. The box starts at I2, the answer starts at I3, and
  `I2:J2` must keep its original contents. Edit A's step 1 ("a cell the instruction names inside the
  box wins… the box's own first row then has to keep its original contents") states exactly this.
  cand_0002's anchor text alone moved this task 0→1, so the mechanism is demonstrated, not predicted.
- **A, does NOT break 50768** — `F12:H14`, a 3×3 matrix, instruction: *"Impact of 1 and Likelihood of
  1 → the **bottom left** box"*. cand_0002's failure was inventing an axis convention while the
  sheet printed its own Impact/Likelihood labels. Edit A's **second bullet** is written against this
  exact failure ("fixed by the labels the sheet prints along the box's edges, plus any orientation
  the instruction states (\"the bottom-left box\" …). Never lay a grid out from a convention … while
  the sheet labels its own axes"), and I dropped the forced prose `ANCHOR:` print that produced the
  invention.
- **A, does NOT break 2768** — the instruction contains a schematic sketch naming column **F** while
  the real destination is `'Sheet1'!H2:H18`. Edit A scopes the naming clause to a cell *"the
  instruction names **inside** the box"*, so F (outside) is never licensed. This scoping is the one
  wording change I made specifically to protect 2768.
- **B, fixes 59595** — `C7:C11` hold real computed integers and the pre-filled `'n/a'` is the **odd
  one out**; the gold answer is a computed number. Branch 2 of Edit B ("odd one out among real
  computed entries → placeholder → overwrite") selects the correct action. Verified in the
  cand_0002 trace that *prose alone* moved this task.
- **B, does NOT break 80-42** — `'Consolidate_ALL'!A2:L8000`, where `"None"` (cols D–I) and `"N/A"`
  (col J) are the convention across ~1000 existing rows. Branch 1 ("the same marker recurs in the
  other rows → it is that table's way of writing 'no value' and you keep it") selects *keep*, and
  the pre-existing absence-convention bullet it cross-references is untouched. Critically,
  *"leave the example cells as they are"* survives **verbatim**, and I added **no** ban on
  `if cell.value is None` — the construct 80-42 passes by.
- **C, fixes 9569** — cand_0001 wrote `round(float(v), 4)`, cand_0002 wrote `v`. I verified the
  mechanism numerically rather than trusting cand_0002's stated rationale (which I had initially
  believed refuted): the grader's `transform_value` does `round(float(v), 2)` on **both** sides, so
  most rows agree either way — but **9 rows land on an `x.xx5` tie that double rounding breaks the
  opposite way**, and one wrong cell scores the task 0. Confirmed by direct computation:

  | gold | → 2 dp | cand_0001's 3–4 dp round | → 2 dp |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | `0.145021572` | `0.15` | `0.145` | `0.14` |
  | `0.075000259` | `0.08` | `0.075` | `0.07` |
  | `0.034966941` | `0.03` | `0.035` | `0.04` |
  | `0.264999741` | `0.26` | `0.265` | `0.27` |

  A subagent independently confirmed gold `AO9 = 0.170687841` (full precision, **not** the owner's
  `0.1707` transcription) against the golden workbook, and that cand_0001 has 9 post-normalisation
  diffs vs cand_0002's 0. So Edit C's rationale is the true mechanism, stated generally.
- **C, does NOT break 38462** — this is the **only** passing val task whose instruction asks for
  rounding (*"round up time … to the nearest whole hour"*). I grepped all 40 val instructions for
  rounding/decimal/precision language to find it. My first draft said "round only when the
  instruction asks for *a set number of decimals*", which would not clearly cover "nearest whole
  hour"; I widened the carve-out to *"Round only when the instruction itself asks you to — 'to the
  nearest whole hour', 'to two decimals', 'as a whole percent' — in which case the rounding is the
  requirement and you apply it."*
- **402-43 needs no edit at all.** It broke under cand_0002 because branch 3 of the verdict table
  sent it hunting outside the box. I dropped that branch; the correct action is *not re-introducing
  the cause*, not adding a counter-rule. (See Deliberately skipped.)
- **Template contract (mechanical, run before anything else)** — reproduced the adapter's own
  validator exactly (`_TEMPLATE_COMMENT_RE.sub(..., count=1)` then `string.Formatter().parse`):
  comment stripped, **all 6 required placeholders present**, `{max_turns}` present, **0 unknown**
  placeholders, `str.format` renders, and **all 4** embedded python blocks `compile()` cleanly with
  braces correctly doubled. One scare worth recording: a naive check flags `{braces}` as an unknown
  placeholder, but it lives inside the leading HTML comment, which `_read_task_template` strips with
  `count=1` **before** parsing — I confirmed that in `adapter.py:868,908` rather than assuming it,
  since an unknown placeholder raises `KeyError` on every task and scores the whole run 0.

## Blast radius — per edit, with the named passing tasks checked

| edit | class | passing tasks in the decision class, and what happens to them |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **A** anchor | **BOUNDED** — only changes behaviour when the box is larger than the answer | **50768** (axis-labels clause is written to protect it), **2768** (naming scoped to *inside* the box), **53647** (`E7:E16` with gold `E15` empty — "any row the answer never reaches keeps its original contents" agrees), **80-42** ("in the first available, blank rows" is the *described place* branch, which points the right way), **382-10**, **142-12**. No rule here fires when the answer fills its box. |
| **B** placeholder | **BOUNDED** — fires only on a pre-filled cell *inside* the box that **contradicts the agent's rule** | **80-42** (branch 1 → keep the column-wide `None`/`N/A` convention → still passes), **382-10**, **53647**. It is a *narrowing condition added to* an existing rule, never a class-wide flip — exactly the DECISION/PERMISSION discipline the diagnose skill prescribes, and the discipline cand_0002 violated. |
| **C** no-rounding | **BOUNDED by enumeration** — I enumerated every val instruction mentioning rounding | **38462** is the only passing task affected, and the widened carve-out explicitly licenses its rounding. For every other task the rule removes an operation that could only ever lose precision. |

Length: `prompt.md` 8585 → 11973 chars, `task_template.md` 168 → 192 lines. For comparison
cand_0002 took the prompt to **13541** chars and the template to 307 lines, and on 80-42 its agent
collapsed into a single silent code block with no prints and no exploration round. Staying well
under that ceiling was a deliberate constraint, not an accident.

**No constraint-bearing line was dropped.** Two rewrites deliberately *weaken* one clause: *"make
your rule reproduce them exactly"* → *"check your rule against them"*, in both files. That is Edit C
itself (the word "exactly" is what drove cand_0001 to round), and the constraint it carried survives
as "agreement is free validation of your reading of the instruction" plus the new digit-count
paragraph. Everything else is pure addition; the formula carve-out, the absence convention, and
*"leave the example cells as they are"* all survive verbatim.

## Deliberately skipped

- **The known-false *"never rename, add, remove or reorder sheets"*** in Rule 3. Passing tasks
  **395-36** and **402-43** both add a sheet and pass, so it is a false statement sitting in the
  prompt — but it **fails the REAL test** (no task fails because of it today), and rewriting a rule
  that two passing tasks already violate harmlessly is an unbounded change for zero expected gain.
  `META_INSIGHTS` flagged it as a spare-capacity item; with 3 tasks in play and a 0.0124 bar, there
  is no spare capacity. Left for a future iteration with headroom.
- **An "an illustration block elsewhere in the sheet is not the deliverable" rule for 402-43.**
  402-43 **currently passes**; the rule would fail the REAL test, and it would also *conflict* with
  the surviving and load-bearing rule that *"an example the user left nearby … wins where the two
  disagree"*. Stacking two rules that give opposite verdicts on the same input is the failure mode
  the capability skill names explicitly. The correct action was removing the cause.
- **Re-proposing the `PLAN` machinery alone**, which `META_INSIGHTS` suggested as the fallback if
  cand_0002 was rejected. I dropped it instead, because the attribution evidence that arrived after
  that note was written contradicts it: `PLAN` was **vacuous on all three fixes** (59595 was fixed in
  the agent's first block, before `PLAN` existed), and on 9569 its `assert` fired on float noise and
  cost a round. Re-proposing it alone would spend an iteration re-measuring something the traces
  already answer.
- **Nothing was skipped for lack of time.** Every cluster the traces show for this iteration got an
  edit, and each of the three regressions got its cause removed.

## Process & features used

- **Six read-only subagents in parallel** for the 1:1 attribution — one per moved task. This was the
  right shape because the six questions are independent and each needs a deep read of two or three
  long traces. The highest-value single finding: 59595's fix landed in the agent's **first** code
  block, which is what falsified `PLAN` as the cause and let me drop the machinery that broke 80-42.
- **A self-correction worth recording.** I initially judged cand_0002's 9569 rationale (the `x.xx5`
  tie story) **refuted**, because I sampled the first ~10 rows of the range and `round(0.1707, 2) ==
  round(0.170687841, 2)` on every one of them. That was a sampling error: the losing rows are at
  39, 49, 310, 574, 578, 592, 630, 893, 1077. A subagent re-ran the full 1280-cell comparison and
  found the 9 ties, and I verified four of them by direct computation before shipping. **Lesson: a
  normalisation that collapses *most* differences does not collapse all of them, and with 1280 cells
  and all-or-nothing grading, 9 is as fatal as 1261 — never refute a mechanism from a sample.**
- **Grounding in source, not feedback strings.** Confirmed from
  `third_party/spreadsheetbench/evaluation/evaluation.py` that colour/fill/font comparison is
  **commented out** (lines 140–151) and only `compare_cell_value` runs — which eliminated my
  competing hypothesis that cand_0001's `number_format = "0.00%"` overwrite caused the 9569 loss, and
  is why Edit C is about rounding and says nothing about formatting. Also re-confirmed that the
  harness feedback *"hold int where float was expected — match the expected type exactly"* is a
  **pre-normalisation diagnostic and is misleading**: `transform_value` sends both `int` and `float`
  through `round(float(v), 2)`, so int-vs-float can never decide a cell.
- **Non-overfitting check, run mechanically at the end — and it caught me.** I grepped both capability
  files for every val task id, every carve-out task id, and the gold values I had quoted while
  reasoning. It fired: my first draft of Edit C illustrated double rounding with
  `round(0.145021572, 2)`, and `0.145021572` is **task 9569's gold value for row 39** — an eval-set
  answer pasted into the prompt, which is exactly what the non-overfitting rule forbids, and the same
  mistake in kind that I criticised cand_0002's `0.1707`/`0.170687841` paragraph for. Replaced with an
  invented value, `round(0.1250004, 2)` is `0.13` vs `0.12` double-rounded, verified to demonstrate
  the identical behaviour. Final grep over both files for task ids, gold values, and sheet names
  (`工作表1`, `Consolidate_ALL`) returns nothing. **Lesson: a value you quoted while diagnosing will
  try to follow you into the prompt — grep for it, don't trust that you'd notice.**
- **Prior iterations read in full** before proposing: `LEDGER.md`, both `JOURNAL.md` entries,
  `INSIGHTS.md`, `META_INSIGHTS.md`, `RUNMAP.md`, `prior_iterations/cand_0001/` and
  `prior_iterations/cand_0002/`, and `rejected.jsonl`. `prior_iterations/cand_0002/diff.patch` is
  **truncated** (literal `... (truncated)` at line 112; the whole `task_template.md` half is
  missing), so I diffed `candidates/cand_0001/*` against `candidates/cand_0002/*` directly — noted
  in `FRAMEWORK_IMPROVEMENTS.md`.
- **Structural difference from `rejected.jsonl`:** cand_0002's rejected entry is the `PLAN`/verdict-
  table/assert batch. This candidate ships **none** of it. The two ideas that genuinely fixed tasks
  are re-proposed with a *narrowing condition attached to each* — which is the structural change,
  not a re-proposal: cand_0002 changed the class-wide rule, this changes only the condition that
  discriminates the failing case from the passing one.
